body:
Random number generators can generate known insecure encryption keys. For some encryption algorithms there are key values known to be vulnerable or insecure (like primes vulnerable to Fermat’s factorization method).

Therefor key generation algorithms exist that avoid generating known vulnerable keys.

A new control should be added to [11.5](https://github.com/OWASP/ASVS/blob/master/5.0/en/0x20-V11-Cryptography.md#v115-random-values) to address the issue:

Verify that cryptographic keys are generated with an approved key generation algorithm for the specific cryptographic algorithm (instead of just a random number generator) to avoid coincidentally generating vulnerable keys. Industry-proven cryptographic key generators should be used.

comments.body:
Big fan of this new requirement.

cc @danielcuthbert @randomstuff
yeah would be keen to get input from @danielcuthbert @randomstuff

I don't disagree. I have not checked it we already have such a requirement.

What is not clear is whether we are talking about secret keys (because of "instead of just a random number generator") or about private keys. It does applies to both.

> What is not clear is whether we are talking about secret keys (because of "instead of just a random number generator") or about private keys. It does applies to both.

@ingo-rauner can you confirm?

We already have:

| # | Description | Level | #v5.0.be |
| :---: | :--- | :---: | :---: |
| **11.6.1** | Verify that only **approved cryptographic algorithms** and modes of operation **are used for key generation** and seeding, and digital signature generation and verification. | 2 | v5.0.be-6.7.2 |

The proposed requirement would split part of 11.6.1 out. I'm not sure we need to (if we want to try limit the number of requirements).
(Interestingly 11.6.1 is listed in "V11.6 Public Key Cryptography" so we are to understand that "key generation" here is about *private key* generation only, and not secret key generation.)

I think we would need to merge this proposal into 11.6.1. 

Is this actually a problem for symmetric keys or only for asymmetric keys? "Fermat’s factorization method" looks like it specifically works for asymmetric so I think maybe it makes sense that this is only in 11.6. What do you think @randomstuff ?

I'm [suggesting](https://github.com/OWASP/ASVS/issues/2590#issuecomment-2817942850) splitting 11.6.1 again in two requirements:

* Verify that only approved cryptographic algorithms are used for digital signature generation and verification.
* Verify that only industry-proven algorithms are used for (private) key generation and (private key) seeding.

If we do that, we can easily change the second as something like:

* Verify that only industry-proven algorithms are used for (private) key generation and (private key) seeding to avoid coincidentally generating vulnerable keys.

I don't think it is worth splitting for that.

I think it would be fine to leave 11.6.1 but explain this potential risk in the section text. e.g.:

## V11.6 Public Key Cryptography

Public Key Cryptography will be used where it is not possible or not desirable to share a secret key between multiple parties.

As part of this, there exists a need for **secure key generation mechanisms, which will not generate insecure keys such as those with primes vulnerable to Fermat’s factorization method as well as secure** ~~approved~~ key exchange mechanisms, such as Diffie-Hellman and Elliptic Curve Diffie-Hellman (ECDH) ~~to ensure that the cryptosystem remains secure against modern threats~~.

If we do want to merge it I would suggest something beefy🥩 like my suggestions below.  I lean towards merging but am not at opposed to @randomstuff wish to split these out.

_11.6.1. Verify cryptographic key generation and digital signature generation and verification must use only approved cryptographic key generation algorithms designed for the intended cryptographic algorithm. This is to ensures keys are not merely random numbers, mitigating the risk of generating vulnerable keys._

> If we do want to merge it I would suggest something beefy🥩 like my suggestions below. I lean towards merging but am not at opposed to [@randomstuff](https://github.com/randomstuff) wish to split these out.
> 
> _11.6.1. Verify cryptographic key generation and digital signature generation and verification must use only approved cryptographic key generation algorithms designed for the intended cryptographic algorithm. This is to ensures keys are not merely random numbers, mitigating the risk of generating vulnerable keys._

Do you disagree with my suggestion here?
https://github.com/OWASP/ASVS/issues/2985#issuecomment-2819336298

> > If we do want to merge it I would suggest something beefy🥩 like my suggestions below. I lean towards merging but am not at opposed to [@randomstuff](https://github.com/randomstuff) wish to split these out.
> > _11.6.1. Verify cryptographic key generation and digital signature generation and verification must use only approved cryptographic key generation algorithms designed for the intended cryptographic algorithm. This is to ensures keys are not merely random numbers, mitigating the risk of generating vulnerable keys._
> 
> Do you disagree with my suggestion here? [#2985 (comment)](https://github.com/OWASP/ASVS/issues/2985#issuecomment-2819336298)

I am sorry to dismiss it. I politely think this is such a big issues that we want a separate requirement for the OP's suggestion.

I also think that adding your suggestion to the 11.6 chapter text is a good idea. This OP's suggest is a very astute observation and I want to make sure it is well covered.

I really want to avoid creating extra requirements where it is absolutely necessary. We already talk about using approved algorithms in 11.6.1 so I don't think we are really adding an extra requirement here but rather adding more explanation about what is needed from an "approved" algorithm. That is why I think it is better to capture it in the section text.

What do you think @randomstuff ?

Avoiding to create too many requirement is indeed an worthwhile goal. Describing the risk of creating weak keys in the section text might work.

The downside is that we should assume that people will skip or skim-read the section text and read more carefully the requirements. By including this information in the section text only, we increase the likelihood that people will not notice this point. That being said it might work.

Another solution is to append an extra sentence in the existing requirement:

> Verify that only approved cryptographic algorithms and modes of operation are used for private key generation and seeding, and digital signature generation and verification. Private key generation algorithms must not generate weak keys such as as RSA keys vulnerable to Fermat factorization.

I'm OK for both solutions.

This extra sentence is elegant enough for me, I opened #3033

This works for now. Thank you for the discussion. Let's hope we don't discover insecure keys for our currently used symmetric algorithms (we had that problem in the past for some symmetric algorithms).
